newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: LASMO sees oil output hike from Venezuela contract.
newsitem.headline: LASMO sees oil output hike from Venezuela contract.

text.p: U.K. oil exploration company LASMO Plc saw great potential to develop Venezuela's Dacion oilfield for which it paid $453 million in a hotly contested bidding competition on Thursday.

Business development manager Roger Tucker said he expected to invest a further $750 million in the 20-year operating contract, hiking oil output from 12,500 barrels per day (bpd) to 90,000 bpd within three to four years.
He said the financing of the project was not yet finalized, but all options remained open and it would not all come from the company's balance sheet.
Tucker said he expected recovery rates from the field to rise from 14 percent to 35 percent, significantly increasing the 289 million barrels of proven reserves.
"LASMO is also confident that considerable exploration potential exists within the Dacion area where no seismic has been shot since the 1950's," Tucker added.
LASMO had spent six months studying opportunities in Venezuela, and four months purely devoted to the Dacion area.
"We saw Dacion as the highest quality asset in this round, we came to get it, we got it, and we won't be bidding any more," Tucker said.
LASMO beat Argentina's Perez Companc to the field by $50 million, both leaving China National Petroleum Corp far behind on $329 million.
Tucker said a technological alliance with U.S.-based Schlumberger would help the company introduce the latest technology to the field and increase recovery rates.

Although the operating contracts are complicated, they offer companies the chance to recoup their investment by giving them 30 percent of the profits from output over the contracted amount, up to a pre-set ceiling.
